issues.description: Field mismatch: class de.tum.cit.ase.Animal field 'name'. The problem statement UML (abstract class Animal) explicitly lists an attribute 'name: String'. In the solution repository, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java declares the field as 'private StringBuilder name;'. This difference in declared type (String vs StringBuilder) forces students to decide between following the UML or the provided solution, and it affects the constructor, getter, and setter types and usage (e.g., getName() is expected to return a String per the spec). This inconsistency is likely to confuse students and may lead to non-uniform implementations or compilation issues if tests expect a String-backed name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal.name attribute type match the problem statement UML by changing the field in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java from StringBuilder to String. Update the constructor to accept a String and assign it directly, and update the getter/setter signatures and bodies to use String. Verify all subclasses and usages (calls to getName(), concatenations, and tests) continue to work with getName() returning a String.
